candidates.title: Data Center-Aware Load Pickup in Power System Restoration
candidates.abstract: Data centers requiring continuous operation rely on onsite generation and battery storage during blackouts. Their return to grid supply must be coordinated with the restoration of other loads because demand fluctuations can affect system frequency. This paper adds constraints to a restoration optimization problem that coordinates load pickup, grid supply to data centers, onsite generation, and battery operation. These constraints reserve battery power and energy to accommodate bounded demand changes while maintaining approved grid supply to data centers. The method accounts for processing delays and checks resource limits using updated operating states before applying commands. Phasor-domain simulations of a low-inertia restoration scenario show that the method serves 760 MW of load outside the data centers and satisfies all tested operating limits. Nominal and frequency-aware benchmarks serve 840 MW and 800 MW, respectively, but violate operating limits.

candidates.title: Torcalia.jl: An MPI-based Runtime System for Asynchronous Task Parallelism in Julia
candidates.abstract: Designed to address the two-language problem, the Julia programming language provides a powerful platform for developing high-performance scientific computing and machine learning applications. Such applications increasingly exhibit irregular, adaptive, or data-driven workloads for which traditional bulk-synchronous parallel (BSP) models often struggle to efficiently exploit the available parallelism. Asynchronous many-task (AMT) runtime systems offer a compelling alternative, decomposing computations into fine-grained tasks that are dynamically scheduled across the hierarchical architecture of modern HPC systems. This paper introduces Torcalia.jl, a Julia package designed to orchestrate the asynchronous execution of tasks across both shared and distributed memory environments. Built on top of MPI.jl and Julia's native multithreading, Torcalia employs a dependency-aware task scheduling scheme that combines the work-sharing and work-stealing paradigms to achieve adaptive load balancing. Tasks can be nested arbitrarily, enabling applications to exploit multiple levels of parallelism, while application-level distributed shared memory (DSM) extends task-based shared-memory programming to multi-node clusters. Beyond task-based programming, the proposed library supports skeletal programming, providing high-level abstractions that facilitate the implementation of parallel applications at scale. Evaluated on the ARIS supercomputer using four diverse workloads, Torcalia demonstrates strong scalability, reducing wall-clock time by up to 18.1% compared with Dagger, a state-of-the-art task-based engine in Julia. The source code of Torcalia.jl is publicly available at https://github.com/CEID-HPCLAB/Torcalia.jl.

candidates.title: GC-MoE K3: A Green-Context Role Graph for Latent Mixture-of-Experts Decode
candidates.abstract: Kimi K3 combines a latent routed mixture of experts with full-width shared experts. A complete feed-forward evaluation must score and select experts, project tokens into the latent space, exchange tokens across expert-parallel ranks, compute the routed and shared branches, and normalize and project the routed sum before joining the branches. We present GC-MoE K3, a datacenter Blackwell implementation that schedules this entire evaluation as a CUDA Graph across two Green Contexts. Five base roles split input projection, routing, dispatch, expert computation, and finalization. Dispatch can fill the routed input ring while the compute partition evaluates shared experts. Finalize waits for the expert owners needed by each token and overlaps routed reduction and RMSNorm with loading the output projection weights. Conditional roles reuse the communication partition for routed computation and reduce split-$K$ projection partials. On GB200 at EP8, EP16, and EP32, the operator is faster at all 24 measured configurations than the paired SGLang-style reference (mean speedup $1.1324\times$). A comparison with historical vLLM-style measurements gives $1.3651\times$ across the same 24 shapes. Both latency comparisons time single-layer graph replay on synthetic K3-shaped inputs with a residual prefix. The separate paired numerical suite passes all 142 cases and 2,936 rank checks.

candidates.title: Voltage Ride-Through-Constrained Power Capping for Large-Scale Data Centers
candidates.abstract: Large-scale data centers may satisfy steady-state network constraints while violating operational limits during voltage disturbances. This paper proposes a voltage ride-through (VRT)-aware power-capping framework that integrates AC optimal power flow scheduling with dynamic ride-through assessment. The proposed dynamic model captures converter limits, DC-link energy dynamics, battery support, and IT-bus voltage response. A simulation-based checker evaluates VRT constraints under prescribed faults, and the power caps are iteratively updated to obtain feasible schedules. Case studies on the IEEE 14-bus system with two data centers demonstrate that steady-state feasible operating points may violate transient voltage and power-import limits. Selective power capping achieves approximately 5\% demand reduction during capped periods while satisfying the prescribed VRT requirements. The results highlight the necessity of incorporating dynamic security assessment into data-center operational limit determination.

candidates.title: Motivo: A Motif-Based Algorithm-Architecture Co-Design for Fast and Energy-Efficient Graph-Based Genome Analysis
candidates.abstract: Read mapping, a key step of genome sequence analysis, matches each fragment of a sequenced genome (a read) to its location in a reference genome. A genome graph is a graph-based reference genome that represents the genetic diversity of a population as alternative paths, and thus improves read mapping accuracy. However, the size and complexity of a genome graph make sequence-to-graph (S2G) mapping a major bottleneck. Prior software and hardware approaches for S2G mapping perform redundant costly operations (e.g., graph traversals and dynamic programming) that do not lead to valid mappings. Our key observation is that a genome graph consists of small subgraphs that share a limited set of recurring topologies, which we call motifs. We propose Motivo, a topology-aware algorithm-architecture co-design for S2G mapping. Motivo's algorithm uses motifs in two ways. First, it stores the precomputed motifs of each node in a compact index, which replaces a graph traversal with a single memory lookup. Second, it uses the topology of a motif and the properties of its nodes to identify the few most suitable mapping paths with arithmetic operations. The algorithm enables high-performance execution on CPUs and GPUs and high-performance, low-energy execution on Motivo-ASIC, an accelerator we co-design with it. Motivo-CPU provides 2.1-18.4x, 2.8-343x, and 1.4-10.1x speedups over GraphAligner, vg, and minigraph, and Motivo-GPU provides 1.5-1.6x speedups over vg-giraffe. Motivo-ASIC provides 7.4-11.7x (138-274x) speedups over state-of-the-art CPU-based tools for short (long) reads. Compared to SeGraM (short reads) and HARP (long reads), Motivo-ASIC achieves 5.3x and 4.0-4.3x higher throughput per Watt and 1.7x and 2.7-3.0x higher throughput per mm$^2$, respectively. Motivo maintains equal or higher mapping accuracy than other tools (96.8%-99.7%) for short and long reads on two types of genome graphs.

A genome graph is a graph-based reference genome that represents the genetic diversity of a population as alternative paths, and thus improves read mapping accuracy. candidates.title: R2WM: Recursive Reasoning Wireless Model for Long-Horizon mmWave Beam Prediction
candidates.abstract: Long-horizon beam prediction aims to extend beam-training intervals while supporting beam alignment in mobile millimeter-wave systems. Although pretrained large models can improve prediction over compact recurrent baselines, their large backbones impose substantial storage and computing requirements. To address this limitation, we propose a recursive reasoning wireless model (R2WM). Given a fixed history of beam indices and angles of departure (AoDs), R2WM repeatedly updates coupled latent and prediction states using a shared causal-attention backbone before jointly decoding the future beam indices. Backbone reuse increases computational depth at fixed parameter count. In the standard 10-step DeepMIMO setting, R2WM achieves an average normalized beamforming gain of 0.9597, compared with 0.8629 for the prompt-as-prefix large language model, with 99.1% fewer parameters and 59.1% fewer counted floating-point operations. Transfer experiments show that R2WM retains normalized gain under the tested carrier-frequency and antenna-count changes, while its beam-index-only variant retains gain under the tested base-station change. Component ablations show higher gains with historical AoD conditioning and causal attention. Recursion analysis reveals a gain-computation trade-off across separately trained configurations with the same parameter count. An additional comparison with a nonrecursive Transformer of similar parameter count shows higher gain for R2WM at greater computational cost. These results support accurate long-horizon beam prediction without a large pretrained backbone.

candidates.title: Energy- and Thermal-Aware Resource Management on Mobile IoT Endpoints: A Survey
candidates.abstract: Energy-aware and thermal-aware management of computing resources on portable and mobile Internet-of-Things (IoT) endpoints is still practiced pillar by pillar: radios, processors, and flash are optimized in isolation, yet sealed system-on-chip (SoC) products share sleep states, interconnects, and thermal limits. Pillar-local joule or temperature gains therefore often disappear after integration, and published savings are frequently incomparable. This survey asks how radio, compute, and storage should be coordinated so that deep sleep remains reachable, and which reporting rules make endpoint energy and thermal claims comparable. We synthesize literature from roughly 2000 to early 2026 with three instruments: a five-phase wireless power anatomy for power-aware networking; a four-branch taxonomy for collective power--performance optimization under mixed regimes; and eight evaluation gates that separate energy outcome, control cost, thermal feasibility, and evidence quality. We qualify the radio-limited premise with compute-, storage-, and thermal-dominated counterexamples, compare modeling and monitoring families, treat thermal behaviour as a shared constraint by separating sensing interfaces, compact models, throttling actuators, and the short-peak versus sustained-throttling regimes that reverse room-temperature rankings, give an illustrative phase-budget example with a sensitivity check and a model-selection workflow, and close with open problems on composability and reproducible measurement. The intended readers work on sustainable computing, mobile systems, and embedded energy management.

candidates.title: Real-Time 250-kHz Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography Using a Jetson AGX Orin
candidates.abstract: High-performance optical coherence tomography (OCT) relies on desktop workstations for data acquisition, reconstruction, and visualization, limiting integration into compact imaging systems. We evaluated whether an embedded GPU platform could sustain real-time operation of a 250-kHz spectral-domain OCT instrument without a desktop computer. A custom C++/CUDA OCT engine running on a NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB was developed and integrated with a 2048-pixel spectrometer, Camera Link frame grabber, and galvanometer scanner, and compared against an RTX A4500 workstation under the same scan protocols. Both systems maintained mean B-scan processing latency well below the corresponding B-scan acquisition intervals. Although the RTX A4500 workstation achieved lower reconstruction latency, Jetson eliminated explicit host-to-device transfer and exhibited more consistent processing latency. Furthermore, the measured active wall power was 67 W for the Jetson and 155 W for the workstation, corresponding to approximately 2.3 times greater wall-energy efficiency for the Jetson. In a separate 62.6-min GUI-enabled measurement, the Jetson processed 800,000 B-scans without frame loss while maintaining real-time reconstruction and visualization. These results demonstrate that embedded computing can support high-speed OCT acquisition, processing, and control while reducing wall-power demand and computing-platform size.

candidates.title: Loadability Assessment for Large-Load Integration: From Repeated Power Flow Tracing to Historical Trajectory Transfer
candidates.abstract: Integrating large data-center loads requires utilities to evaluate voltage-stability loading margins under different generation and demand conditions. Continuation power flow (CPF) traces P--V curves through successive prediction and correction steps, but related assessments can repeatedly reconstruct similar nonlinear behavior. Reusing an operating point as an initial guess does not capture the subsequent voltage response. This paper proposes a continuation method that transfers finite segments of historical power flow (PF) trajectories. Each segment is aligned with the present state and continuation direction, supplementing the CPF tangent predictor with previously computed nonlinear curve shape. Short Newton tests evaluate compatibility with the present PF equations, and an attention-based selector combines their results with network conditions, loading patterns, and recent continuation states. Numerical correction and fold refinement determine accepted solutions and the loading limit. The analysis bounds prediction error through differences in trajectory curvature and establishes sufficient conditions for local correction and branch preservation. Studies on modified IEEE 14- and 118-bus systems under renewable-generation and data-center load variations demonstrate reduced online computation and higher observed recovery of specified continuation solutions than Adaptive CPF. For loading-limit assessment, paired online speedups are 4.88--21.62$\times$ over Adaptive CPF and 1.53--4.77$\times$ over holomorphic embedding with arc-length parametrization (HEAP) across the tested scenarios.
